cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Choose What Matters More
cards.instruction: Make someone choose between emotional safety and the outcome they claim to want.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. They're calling your audition number. Do you want the part enough to let them hear you?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I want it. I don't want them laughing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. I can walk you in or drive you home. Which want am I helping?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Walk me in, but promise they won't laugh.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can promise I'll stay. Is that enough to risk the audition, or are we going home?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 and A3 status prefixes do not materially change the equal-helper choice offers; A5 I can promise still lacks distinct superior approval behavior.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 wants role without laughter causes A3 walk/home choice; B4 requests both via guarantee, causing A5 support-only promise and renewed trade-off.

relationship.evidence: B2 fear is credible and B4 chooses audition conditionally, creating the exact conflict A must clarify.

heightening.evidence: B4 impossible guarantee causes A5 a real promise of presence while preserving emotional risk.

specificity.evidence: A1 number called and B2 desired role establish immediate stakes; no actual hostile panel is asserted.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 staying promise is earned and clear, but the generic rank clauses are not a merged tactic.
